feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with strategy/content/platform roles. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat repetitive and dense, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression and credibility: multiple promotions within NACo strongly signal performance, trust, and increasing leadership scope.  
- Good impact evidence: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.  
- Strong positioning: headline, summary, and skills consistently support a digital strategy/communications leadership brand.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten redundancy: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap heavily; consolidate to save space and improve structure.  
- Add more outcome-focused metrics beyond scope/activity, especially for email, social, video, and consulting work (growth, engagement, efficiency, cost/time savings).  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: use “12 years of experience” (not “12 years experience”); standardize serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement”); consider consistent capitalization for “full-time”; “Coleman DAVIS” may look stylistically inconsistent unless intentional.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. Tightening the language and adding a sharper leadership/value angle would improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Lead with your seniority and strongest differentiators: digital strategy, platform modernization, and operational systems for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Reduce the long channel list; “multi-channel” or “cross-channel” already covers web, email, social, and multimedia.
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience driving multi-channel programs, platform modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in digital strategy, editorial workflow design, stakeholder coordination, and translating complex policy or technical issues into clear, audience-focused communications. Strong track record leading web, email, social, and multimedia ecosystems that improve reach, usability, and organizational effectiveness.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and channel-specific lists overlap with Core Competencies.
- “Stakeholder coordination” and workflow/systems language are repeated elsewhere; keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Soft Skills. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing higher-value leadership capabilities will make it more distinctive and senior.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace generic terms with sharper, senior-level language: “Multi-channel communications leadership” instead of “Multi-channel communication,” and “Web platform governance & CMS administration” instead of “Web & CMS administration.”
- Consolidate overlapping items: “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture” could become “Editorial operations, workflow & systems design.”
- Prioritize the most marketable strengths first: digital strategy, web platform modernization, editorial operations, analytics, and advocacy/public-sector communications.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Web platform governance & CMS administration • Editorial operations, workflow & systems design • Multi-channel communications leadership • Data analytics, reporting & optimization • Stakeholder & cross-functional coordination • Policy & advocacy communications • Multimedia, video & live event production

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with the header summary and Topline Skills; consider shortening this section or using it only for broad themes not repeated elsewhere.
- “Stakeholder & cross-department coordination” also overlaps with Soft Skills.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Make it sharper by emphasizing this engagement’s distinct outcomes, technical depth, and flagship initiatives.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a tighter positioning line: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements, campaign delivery, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, implemented, established.
- Consolidate into 4–5 bullets focused on outcomes, e.g. Drupal campaign builds, cross-channel governance/workflows, analytics/reporting systems, AI-enabled search initiative.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages/templates, users, teams supported, workflow time saved, engagement lift, search accuracy/adoption, toolkit downloads.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “digital strategy, governance, analytics, workflows” repeats the summary and NACo Director role; keep only what is new in this consulting engagement.
- The microsite and AI search bullets overlap with “Recent Projects”; either keep this entry high-level or make the project blurbs more specific.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-scope leadership entry with good platform and scale detail. It will be stronger if you tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation wins, and add clearer outcomes for channels, studio, and analytics.

Suggested edit
- Replace the broad lead sentence with a sharper scope line: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Prioritize the highest-impact bullets first: website migration, analytics modernization, then studio build and channel leadership.
- Add outcome language where possible: “migrated 10,000+ pages to Drupal for 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ publishers” and quantify newsletter/social growth, engagement, production volume, or cost savings if available.
- Tighten weaker phrasing: change “serving thousands of followers” to a metric-driven result; change “improving reporting and strategic decision-making” to a specific benefit like faster reporting, better campaign insight, or executive dashboards.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the prior NACo role; emphasize enterprise leadership, transformation, and infrastructure here instead of day-to-day channel management.
- Video studio/buildout may partially overlap with earlier video-production bullets; frame this as scaling in-house capability, not producing recurring content.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story within NACo, but this entry overlaps heavily with the adjacent NACo roles. Make it more distinct by emphasizing operational leadership, editorial coordination, and channel growth before you became director.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving coordination of advocacy and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground ownership: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Launched and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing with clearer impact: “Built cross-team editorial planning processes across communications, advocacy and program staff, improving publishing consistency and campaign coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital communications across web, email, social and video” repeats the Director role; here, stress day-to-day operations and process-building instead of overall leadership.
- “Weekly video updates” also appears in the prior NACo role; frame this version as scaling/operationalizing the format.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this topline item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. Make it sharper, more senior, and more clearly tied to recent enterprise-scale leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with higher-signal wording tied to scope: “Enterprise digital strategy & transformation” instead of “Enterprise digital strategy.”
- Tighten and elevate the list to emphasize leadership and governance:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Keep wording parallel and concise; avoid mixing nouns (“strategy”) with broader phrases (“audience-focused content planning”).
- If space allows elsewhere, add scale-based proof near this section or in recent roles (e.g., 10,000+ page Drupal migration, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) rather than here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicates “Multi-channel communication” in Core Competencies.
- “Editorial systems and governance” overlaps with “Editorial workflow design” and “Workflow & systems architecture.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. Make this more strategic and recent-impact oriented by grouping skills around execution strengths rather than naming every platform.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented categories, e.g.: “Drupal and CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based content systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Put Drupal first and keep AI-enabled search, since both are reinforced by the most recent roles.
- Cut lower-priority platform names here if they already appear elsewhere; this section should signal strengths, not repeat the inventory.
- Consider replacing “Power Pages” and possibly “SharePoint” with a broader phrase like “enterprise web platforms” unless those tools were central in recent work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT” entries for Web Platforms & CMS and Coding & Technical Implementation.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with the Automation & Workflow Systems section.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list for recent leadership roles, but it reads as a generic inventory rather than a value-focused skills line. Tighten it around analysis-to-decision impact and align wording with the strongest recent experience.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Analytics strategy & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity, KPI framework design, executive reporting, SEO and digital performance analysis.”
- Put the highest-signal, most recent tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, then Clarity.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If accurate, strengthen “SEO and performance analysis” to “SEO, UX and conversion performance analysis” or “search, content and user-behavior analysis.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo bullet on analytics infrastructure; keep this item tool/capability-focused, not achievement-focused.
- Avoid adding Google Tag Manager here since it already appears under Technical + IT.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads generic and underplays your recent leadership-level multimedia work. Tighten it to emphasize studio buildout, broadcast-quality production, and hybrid event delivery tied to recent NACo experience.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic terms with higher-value phrasing: “Broadcast-quality video production,” “livestream and hybrid event delivery,” “PTZ camera and studio systems,” “virtual event operations.”
- Reorder by impact/recency: lead with studio and event delivery, then production/editing.
- Consider a tighter version: “Broadcast-quality video production & editing • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio systems • Virtual event operations”
- If space allows, add scale/context instead of tools alone, e.g. “In-house studio production” or “Recurring advocacy and event programming.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production”; keep this version more specific/technical.
- Avoid repeating “video production” language already covered in older NACo roles unless this skills line adds sharper specialization.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” This section should either be more concise or add signal through recency/specialization.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent relevance: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider emphasizing depth: **Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers instead of just names: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; custom microsites), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages**
- Keep formatting consistent with other technical lists; commas may read cleaner than bullets in ATS parsing.
- If GitHub Pages was minor compared with enterprise CMS work, consider dropping it to keep the list sharper and more senior.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section almost exactly.
- “CMS modernization” already appears elsewhere, so avoid repeating that phrase here unless replacing the topline entry.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools most relevant to recent Drupal/CMS modernization work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End & Technical Implementation**
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **JavaScript • HTML5 • CSS3 • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions**
- Consider dropping **jQuery** or moving it to the end as legacy support, unless it is still actively used in current consulting work.
- If space allows, add a qualifier for impact/context: **Front-end development for Drupal/CMS environments • API integrations • deployment/automation tooling**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution** (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”). Keep one section broader and this one more tool-specific.
- “Workflow automation” already appears elsewhere; avoid implying the same capability here unless tied specifically to **GitHub Actions**.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow systems capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize application, e.g. **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems**.
- Group by function for faster scanning: **Automation:** Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | **Project/work management:** Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | **Team collaboration:** Slack, Teams.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: **used to support editorial planning, cross-team coordination, and process automation**.
- Consider trimming weaker/older tools if not current; keep the most relevant to recent roles first: **Airtable, Power Automate, Jira, Asana, Slack, Teams**.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating them without added context.
- Listing too many PM/chat tools can dilute impact unless they reflect current, hands-on use.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent roles, this line should emphasize platform fluency and engagement systems rather than repeat channel ownership.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add functional scope instead of only listing tools: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • newsletter operations, audience segmentation, journey setup, campaign deployment**
- Keep this item platform-focused and let work experience carry scale/impact; only add metrics here if they are platform-specific and not repeated elsewhere.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already covered in NACo experience.
- “Engagement” may overlap with Core Competencies and Topline Skills, so use this section to list systems/tools, not strategy language.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and foundational, emphasizing team-building, production, and platform support rather than leadership already covered later.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to stress early-career scope: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and support daily web, email, social, and multimedia operations.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh scope, livestream/event volume, cadence/views for weekly videos, or growth/efficiency gains.
- Tighten phrasing: replace “high-impact digital content” with specific deliverables like “livestreamed events, weekly advocacy videos, and web/social content.”
- Clarify supervision modestly: “provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” or “helped onboard/support…”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; if kept here, frame this as launching or initially producing the series.
- “strengthening workflows across web, email, social…” risks repeating later governance/operations bullets; keep this at a support/buildout level.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch and cross-functional project support, while trimming generic research/production phrasing.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the standout outcome: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched the organization’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrases like “contributed to digital content production” with clearer ownership: “developed multimedia and digital content assets” or “supported production of program and policy communications materials.”
- If possible, add scope: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles so progression is clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later digital/media roles; avoid repeating broad multimedia language.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here, since management appears more credibly in 2015–2024 roles.
